Use case: precise-object-edit.
Edit the supplied Havenline SELF-SERVICE COUNTER four-panel sheet. Preserve the current approved small unit sizes, Character1/customer appearance, timber table, warm peach background, all four panels/headings, low solid ORANGE conveyor housings, thick YELLOW rims, dense black rollers, silver bridge plates and blue base. No register and no clerk. Food shown is current eligible meal presentation; cash remains separate.
Repair ONLY these concrete state/consistency defects:
1. An OPEN/READY gate must be physically OPEN. In both upper panels and in lower-left READY panel, rotate the hinged black/yellow stop arm upward to a clearly VERTICAL raised position beside the post so the entire roller lane is unobstructed. Green lamp. It cannot remain a horizontal barrier in a ready panel.
2. Lower-right FULL / RESTOCK WAITS: show the stop arm CLOSED horizontally across the incoming lane, with an amber lamp. Extend a short supported incoming roller stub BEHIND the gate. Put the waiting meal tray fully on that upstream stub BEFORE the closed bar, visibly prevented from entering. Keep the curved lane between gate and table empty or clear; the table stock landing is full with three same-size meals. No tray straddles the barrier. Give the stock landing a subtle low silver outer lip that contains items without blocking customer access.
3. The separate cash pad must stay at the physical END OF THE TABLE OPPOSITE THE CONVEYOR in every angle. In upper-left CUSTOMER SIDE, the conveyor is at image-right, so move the cash pad to the table's far image-left end. In upper-right and lower panels, the conveyor is image-left and cash remains at the far image-right end. Keep the cash pad off the food transfer plate. Same small green bundles as before, no enlargement.
Keep the customer autonomously collecting a meal, and C1 visiting with a small carried stack. Do not change geometry, scale, stock unit identity, add random people, cash registers, text paragraphs, phone UI, machinery, or new products. This is a targeted repair of the same sheet, not a redesign.
